summary: Backend brand-delete OTP flow validated end-to-end via pytest (8/8 passing) including addCompany, missing-otp 400, non-owned 403, send-otp response shape (masked email + preview_otp + expires_in=600), 5-strike lockout invalidating the code, correct-otp delete (rowsDeleted=1), repeat-delete 403/404, and hero-image endpoints (trash.png / check.png / key-off.png). Verified via backend logs the SUPPRESSED emails with subjects 'Confirm brand deletion – <name>' and 'Brand deleted – <name>' and 'Your brand profile was updated'. Frontend UI test uncovered a HIGH-severity bug in the /settings page: after switching the brand via the header company-selector, the inline CompanySettingsDialog + DeleteBrandModal still target the previously-selected (first) brand — so 'QA Throwaway Brand' shown in the header but the modal reads 'This permanently removes The Dev Store … Type The Dev Store to continue'. This is a data-loss risk (a user believing they are deleting a QA brand could delete the primary 'The Dev Store'). QA-created brand id=175 was cleaned up via API to keep the account at 4 brands as required. Code-level verification of checkout de-dup: CleanCheckoutV2.tsx no longer references clean-checkout-crypto-split; breakdownRows.ts adds crypto `sub` lines on merchant/fee rows when split+code exist (lines 62, 86, 90) — confirmed. /pay/demo does not render CleanCheckoutV2 (it is a mirror page with its own testids), so UI-level assertion of clean-checkout-fee-breakdown was only possible via code.

ui_bugs.issue: Header company-selector changes globalSelectedId, but the settings page's local `selectedId` state only initializes from globalSelectedId — never re-syncs. As a result, the inline Account-details form and Delete-brand modal keep operating on the FIRST loaded brand even after the user switches brands via the header. In the reproduction: header shows 'QA Throwaway Brand' but modal body says 'This permanently removes The Dev Store' and 'Type The Dev Store to continue'. This is a data-loss risk.
Page <title> reports 'Settings · Dynopay' on /settings?section=company; review request expected 'Brand Settings · Dynopay'.

action_items: HIGH: Fix pages/settings/index.tsx so that changing the header company-selector re-syncs `selectedId` (or use `globalSelectedId` directly for the inline CompanySettingsDialog). Current effect only initializes selectedId once — subsequent header changes are ignored and delete/edit will silently target the wrong brand.
LOW: If 'Brand Settings · Dynopay' is intended for the /settings?section=company page, update the Next.js <Head><title> accordingly (currently 'Settings · Dynopay').

OPTIONAL: /pay/demo mirrors CleanCheckoutV2 with a separate implementation (pages/pay/demo.tsx). Consider either (a) unifying it with CleanCheckoutV2 or (b) porting the fee-breakdown testids to demo so future regression on the double-breakdown bug can be caught by demo UI tests.
critical_code_review_comments: pages/settings/index.tsx L166-171: the guard `(selectedId === null || !companies.some(c=>c.company_id===selectedId))` prevents re-sync when header company-selector changes globalSelectedId. Rewrite to always follow globalSelectedId (with a valid-id check) so /settings mirrors the header selection.

DeleteBrandModal correctly reads `companyName` from props — the bug is upstream (wrong `company` prop passed while header shows a different brand). Consider passing `companyId+companyName` from the CompanyDataContext's active selection instead of the settings page's local state to avoid drift.

Backend OTP lockout returns 'Verification code expired or not found. Please request a new one.' after the 5th failed attempt, not the 'Too many incorrect attempts' string described in the review request. Behaviourally equivalent (code is invalidated) but the copy differs; align UX message if the intent was 'Too many attempts'.

rca of the issue: pages/settings/index.tsx keeps `selectedId` in local component state and initializes it from `companyState.selectedCompanyId` on mount only. The initialization effect's guard skips re-runs whenever `selectedId` corresponds to a known company. Because the header CompanySelector mutates `companyState.selectedCompanyId` (globalSelectedId) directly in the Zustand store, the settings page ignores those updates. Consequence: the inline CompanySettingsDialog receives an outdated `company` prop → DeleteBrandModal's `companyName` shows the wrong brand → the confirm-input and delete request target the first brand instead of the one the user intends. Mitigation: replace the guarded init effect with an unconditional sync on globalSelectedId change (validated against `companies`) or read directly from `companyState.selectedCompanyId` when deriving `selectedCompany`.
